slot.brief: Compare elongation or breaking condition of two wires of same material but different lengths/radii under the same load; ask the ratio of elongations using Young's modulus.

stem: Wire A has length $L$ and radius $r$. Wire B is made by drawing A to four times its length, without loss of material. Under the same tensile force, what is the ratio of their elongations, $\frac{\Delta\ell_B}{\Delta\ell_A}$?

verdicts.working: With volume conserved, wire B has length 4L and cross-sectional area A/4. Since Δℓ = FL/(AY), its elongation is 4/(1/4) = 16 times that of A.

working:
$A_B(4L)=A_A L\Rightarrow A_B=A_A/4$; $\Delta\ell=FL/(AY)\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta\ell_B}{\Delta\ell_A}=\dfrac{4L/A_B}{L/A_A}=16$.

Independent check: With volume conserved, wire B has length 4L and cross-sectional area A/4. Since Δℓ = FL/(AY), its elongation is 4/(1/4) = 16 times that of A.
solution:
Conservation of volume gives $A_B(4L)=A_A L$, hence $A_B=A_A/4$. Using $\Delta\ell=FL/(AY)$ under the same force and material,
$$\frac{\Delta\ell_B}{\Delta\ell_A}=\frac{4L/A_B}{L/A_A}=16.$$
